cover.headline: Two strong businesses, four ordinary ones, and a price that already assumes the turnaround works
cover.lead: Godrej Agrovet is India's largest cattle-feed maker and largest crude palm oil producer, with crop protection, a loss-making listed chemicals arm (Astec), a South Indian dairy and a chicken brand attached. In FY26 oil palm and feed earned 71% of segment EBITDA; dairy and foods earned 9% on 22% of revenue. Q1FY27 showed the swings: feed EBIT +30%, oil palm +14%, but crop care −38% after a dry June, and attributable profit fell 17%. A new CEO (from Sep-2025) is pruning the portfolio. We value the company the way the street does, as a **sum of the parts on Sep-28E EV/EBITDA (blended 11.4x), with Astec at market value less 20%**. That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** P/E on the stock's own de-rated history (₹785) is higher, the DCF (₹537) lower. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Oil palm is the best business, and a price-taker
arguments.p: Vegetable Oil earned ₹428 cr of EBITDA in FY26 (21.4% margin, ~66% return on segment capital) as FFB volume rose 19% and CPO realisations 9%. Q1FY27 CPO was ₹1,34,783/t (+18%), inflated by the Middle East war. Farmers are paid by a CPO-linked formula and domestic prices follow import costs: on 24-Sep-2026 the government halved the duty on crude palm oil (10% to 5%). We model margins of 20.5% / 19.5% / 19.5%; every point is ~₹1.0 of FY28E EPS.

arguments.h: Feed is a volume winner with thin margins
arguments.p: Animal Nutrition sold 16.5 lakh t in FY26 (+12%; cattle feed +18%) and earned an 8.3% EBITDA margin, helped by Q4 commodity buying and pet-food manufacturing income. Management guides EBIT of ₹2,050-2,150 a tonne; we model 8.0-8.1%. Part of the working-capital gain is supplier financing: payables rose ₹766 cr in FY26.

arguments.h: Crop care is shrinking and Astec still loses money
arguments.p: Standalone crop care EBIT fell from ₹308 cr (FY25) to ₹224 cr (FY26) and 38% in Q1FY27, as the cotton herbicide franchise met bad weather and new in-licensed products earn less. Astec lost ₹81 cr in FY26 (₹135 cr in FY25); its structure is "under evaluation". We model crop care margins of 28-30% (not the 40%+ of FY25) and a slow Astec recovery.

Brokers use SOTP: Motilal Oswal ₹675 (10-11x FY28E EV/EBITDA, Aug-2026). Our multiples come from the stock's own forward EV/EBITDA median since 2021 (15.4x) less the peers' 26% de-rating. Our FY28E EPS of ₹31.8 is 12% below Motilal Oswal's ₹36.0. At ₹624 the stock trades at 19.6x our FY28E EPS.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): Crop Care's FY27 outlook, which management promised once the cotton-herbicide season was clear (end-September).
Domestic CPO prices after the 24-Sep-2026 duty cut on crude palm oil (10% to 5%): the biggest swing factor for oil-palm margins.
Astec: the group said in May-2026 it would decide the "most optimal structure" for Astec and its chemicals business within two to three quarters.
Specialty-fats refinery ramp-up in H2FY27 and the integrated palm complex: the start of the downstream (value-added) strategy.
Milk procurement costs (Creamline) and the route-to-market reset; Godrej Foods' branded growth vs live-bird run-down.

sections.title: Six businesses under one roof, with very different economics

blocks.p: Godrej Agrovet (GAVL) sells to farmers and buys from farmers. **Animal Nutrition** makes compound feed for dairy cattle (55-56% of volume), poultry, fish and shrimp. **Vegetable Oil** buys fresh fruit bunches (FFB) from ~80,000 ha of oil palm planted by farmers in factory zones allotted by state governments, and crushes them into crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel oil. **Crop Care** sells branded herbicides, insecticides and plant-growth regulators (Hitweed for cotton, Gracia for chilli, new Ashitaka, Takai, Ghassnash) and consolidates 67%-owned **Astec LifeSciences**, a listed maker of agrochemical active ingredients and contract manufacturer (CDMO). **Dairy** is Creamline (Godrej Jersey milk, curd, paneer, flavoured milk in the South). **Poultry & processed foods** is Godrej Foods (Real Good Chicken, Yummiez). It also owns 50% of ACI Godrej Agrovet, a Bangladeshi feed maker (revenue ₹1,501 cr, profit ₹80 cr in FY26).

blocks.p: **Feed** is a conversion business: maize, soymeal and rice bran go in, feed comes out at ₹2,000-2,200 of EBIT a tonne; margins move with commodity prices and how fast they can be passed on. **Oil palm** earns a share of the CPO price: the state fixes the monthly price paid for FFB by a formula linked to CPO, so when CPO rises the mill keeps part of the gain, and the reverse. Oil extraction (18.8% in Q1FY27) and volume are the levers it controls. **Crop care** earns 30-45% margins on in-house molecules sold through dealers, but sales are packed into a few weeks of the kharif season. **Dairy and poultry** buy milk and birds at market prices and sell branded products; margins are thin until brands carry a premium.

blocks.callout: **What it means for the numbers:** the minorities that mattered (49% of Godrej Foods, 37-48% of Creamline) are gone, so from FY26 almost all minority interest is Astec's 32.97%, which absorbs a third of Astec's losses. That is why profit attributable to owners (₹473 cr) was higher than total profit (₹445 cr) in FY26. If Astec turns profitable the effect reverses.

sections.title: Five markets, one common thread: farm commodities and the monsoon set the margin

blocks.p: GAVL does not sit in one industry. It buys and sells farm commodities in five markets, and in each the margin depends on prices it does not set. **Feed** competes with home-mixed feed and many regional players; costs are maize and soymeal, and maize now also feeds ethanol distilleries. **Palm oil** is the one market where India is short: domestic crude palm oil output was 3.80 lakh t in 2024-25 against a national target of 11.2 lakh t, so prices follow imports, and imports follow world prices and Indian duties. **Crop protection** is seasonal and monsoon-timed. **Dairy** is a procurement game: when milk is scarce, processors pay more than they can pass on. **Chicken** is mostly sold live and unbranded; branded frozen chicken is new.

sections.title: Animal Nutrition: market-beating volume, commodity-sized margins

bullets: **Volume leader.** 16.5 lakh t sold in FY26 (+12%) and 4.0 lakh t in Q1FY27 (+7%), with cattle feed +18% and +15%. Management says it is gaining share in East and Central India and that high milk prices push farmers to branded feed. Poultry feed is being cut in chosen regions; fish feed (~7% of volume) grew 20%+.

**Margins move with commodities.** Segment EBITDA margin: 5.2% (FY20), 7.6% (FY21), 6.5% (FY22), 4.6% (FY23), 5.9% (FY24), 7.5% (FY25), 8.3% (FY26). Reported EBIT per tonne was ₹2,109 in FY26; guidance is ₹2,050-2,150. Q4FY26's 10.4% included ~₹9.5 cr of pet-food manufacturing income (for Godrej Pet Care, a group company), and Q1FY27 had 'smart' maize buying that management says "may not be exactly structural".

**Supplier financing.** From FY26 the segment pays for vendor invoice discounting inside its costs (reported Q1FY27 EBIT ₹84 cr vs underlying ₹102 cr). Segment liabilities rose from ₹648 cr to ₹1,379 cr, so capital employed fell to ₹251 cr and the reported ROCE (138.6%) is not meaningful.
**Strategy.** From "feed" to "nutrition": premium cattle feed, technical service, geographic expansion; shrimp feed under strategic review; broiler feed to be restricted.

We model revenue +11% / +9% / +8% (FY27-29E) and EBITDA margin 8% / 8% / 8.1%, i.e. EBIT per tonne in the guided range, not the Q4FY26 peak. Upside: premium mix and a softer maize market. Risk: a commodity spike like FY23 (margin 4.6%).

sections.title: Oil palm: a structural growth business with a price-linked margin

pair.title: Revenue by quarter (ex trading)

pair.title: Segment margin: 16.7% in Q1FY27 vs 18.9%

bullets: **Volume engine.** ~80,000 ha of farmer plantations; 17,000 ha added in FY26 and the same targeted for FY27; plan to reach ~1,50,000 ha (Telangana, North-East). About half the trees are 0-4 years old: yields rise steeply from year 4 to year 8, which management calls a "demographic dividend". FFB processed ~6.37 lakh t a year; FFB growth guided at high single to early double digits for 4-5 years.
**Efficiency.** Oil extraction ratio improved 70 bp in FY26 and was 18.8% in Q1FY27 (18.4%); 24 farmer service centres; boilers run on fruit-bunch residue.

**Price.** Farmers are paid a monthly state-set price linked to CPO, so the mill keeps a share of price moves. CPO realisation: ₹1,03,708/t (FY25), ₹1,12,781/t (FY26), ₹1,34,783/t (Q1FY27). Management said ~65-70% of FY26's profit jump came from its own efforts and ~30% from price. A formula change cut Q1FY27 margins; the 24-Sep-2026 duty cut (crude palm oil 16.5% to 11% all-in) lowers the landed price of imports by ~4.7% at unchanged world prices.

**Downstream.** Specialty-fats refinery from H2FY27; integrated palm complex (nursery, mill; seed garden and refinery to follow). Target: 50-55% of the business in value-added products by FY31, adding ~200 bp to group EBITDA margin "when fully scaled". Half of group capex goes here; hurdle IRR 16-18%.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the best business in the group, and the one investors pay for. But FY26-27 profits are flattered by war-time prices. We model revenue +18% / +6% / +10% and EBITDA margin 20.5% / 19.5% / 19.5% (FY26 21.4%; FY21 15.4%), i.e. volume growth with prices easing from FY28. Every 1 point of margin moves FY28E EPS by ~₹1.0 (~3%). A fall back to FY21's 15.4% margin would cut FY28E EPS by ~₹4.0 (~13%).

sections.title: Crop Care and Astec: a high-margin franchise in a soft patch, and a chemicals arm still losing money

pair.title: Standalone crop care revenue by quarter

pair.title: Standalone EBIT margin: 45% to 32% in two years (Q1)

bullets: **The franchise.** Standalone revenue ₹764 cr (FY25) and ₹772 cr (FY26) at 40% and 29% EBIT margins. Profit is concentrated in in-house cotton herbicide (Hitweed) and the chilli insecticide Gracia, sold in a few weeks of the season. FY26 suffered unseasonal rain, lower cotton acreage and channel stock; Q1FY27 a 40% June rain deficit (revenue −17%, EBIT −38%).

**Diversification.** Ashitaka (maize herbicide), Takai (insecticide, paddy plus five crops) and Ghassnash (soybean herbicide, May-2026) were ~18-20% of Q1FY27 sales vs ~3% in FY26. They are in-licensed, so margins are lower than Hitweed's. Management targets a 26-27% standalone EBIT margin for FY27 and would give a fuller view only after September.

**Astec LifeSciences (67.03%, listed).** Revenue ₹628 cr (FY23), ₹381 cr (FY25), ₹448 cr (FY26); losses ₹47 cr, ₹135 cr and ₹81 cr in FY24-26 (Screener). FY26 EBITDA broke even (company basis); Q1FY27 revenue ₹83 cr (−9%), EBITDA nil. CDMO is ~52% of revenue and exports ~53%. GAVL put ₹199 cr into a rights issue in Jul-2025; the board was reshaped in 2026 and the group is reviewing Astec's structure. Its 30-Sep-2026 market value was ~₹1,620 cr (₹722.75 a share).

blocks.callout: **Our view:** crop care is still a very profitable business, but not the 40%+ margin business of FY25: the new products dilute margins and the weather risk is high. We model standalone revenue +3% / +12% / +10% and EBITDA margin 28% / 30% / 30% (our basis: crop care less Astec). Astec: revenue +15% / +15% / +12% at 3% / 7% / 9% EBITDA margins, i.e. still loss-making after interest in FY27-28. In the SOTP we take Astec at its market value less 20%: ₹869 cr, ~₹45 a share.

bullets: **Dairy (Creamline, 'Godrej Jersey').** Revenue ₹1,501 cr (FY23) to ₹1,589 cr (FY26); segment EBITDA margin 2.6%, 3.7%, 0.4%, -0.8%, 4.2%, 5%, 3.6% (FY20-26). Value-added products rose to 49% of sales in Q1FY27 and volume grew 8%, but milk procurement prices and war-led packaging costs cut EBITDA to ₹7 cr. GAVL paid ₹922 cr in FY25-26 to own 99.78%; Creamline earned ₹3 cr of profit in FY26. A new CEO is redoing the route to market over 18-20 months.

**Godrej Foods (Real Good Chicken, Yummiez).** Revenue ₹1,003 cr (FY23) to ₹768 cr (FY26) as live-bird trading is cut 15-20% a year; branded B2C is ~32% of the business and grows ~20% (Yummiez volume +22% in Q1FY27). EBITDA ₹50 cr in FY26, ₹5 cr in Q1FY27 as costs rose and advertising stepped up. Management expects 3-4 years of investment; target 65-70% B2C.
**Synergies are thin.** Management admits it has not linked Creamline's milk farmers to its cattle-feed sales; the businesses mostly share a parent, not customers.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** two turnarounds with good brands and poor economics: Creamline's return on segment capital was 4.6% and Godrej Foods' 9.9% in FY26. We model dairy EBITDA margins of 2.5% / 3.5% / 4% and foods 5% / 6% / 6.5%, i.e. a recovery to FY24-25 levels, not beyond. Together they are ~₹{{F.seg.dairy.adjEbitda.2|num}} cr + ₹{{F.seg.food.adjEbitda.2|num}} cr of FY29E EBITDA.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: real in oil palm and feed scale, absent in pricing

verdicts: 16.5 lakh t of feed (FY26), volume +12% vs the market; commodity buying and R&D formulation let it beat industry growth and hold ₹2,000+ EBIT per tonne.
~80,000 ha of farmer plantations in allotted factory zones, best-in-class OER (18.8% in Q1FY27), 24 Samadhan farmer centres; zones are allotted by states and take 4-8 years to mature.
Crop care brands and in-house molecules
30-45% EBIT margins on Hitweed (cotton herbicide) and Gracia; but concentrated in two crops, and new in-licensed products earn less.
Feed passes on only 60-70% of cost; palm-oil margins follow CPO prices and import duties; dairy passes on ~70% of milk costs.
Godrej Jersey and Yummiez are regional/early; dairy margins (2-5%) are half of listed peers'.
Keeps GAVL competitive; does not set it apart.
Losses in FY24-26 (₹47 cr, ₹135 cr, ₹81 cr); 47% of imports from China; CDMO pipeline unproven.
CRISIL A1+; adjusted gearing 0.81x after the Creamline buyout; group lowers funding cost.
Keeps GAVL competitive; does not set it apart.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard
blocks.source: GAM research compilation (company filings and calls to Sep-2026)

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** GAVL has **two genuine advantages**: the oil-palm franchise (state-allotted factory zones, farmer relationships built over decades, the best extraction rates in India, and plantations that take 4-8 years to replicate) and scale and sourcing skill in cattle feed. Crop care has a strong brand but a narrow product base. Dairy, chicken and Astec have **no moat today**. None of the businesses sets its own prices: feed and dairy pass on 60-70% of costs, oil palm earns a formula-linked share of a world price, and Indian import duties can move that price overnight. Expect a 15-20% ROE company whose profits swing with commodity cycles, not a compounding consumer franchise.

sections.title: Revenue has tripled since FY15; the margin has stayed stuck at 7-9%

blocks.p: Godrej Agrovet's revenue rose from ₹3,312 cr in FY15 to ₹10,233 cr in FY26, 10% a year over the last five years. Profit has grown more slowly and less smoothly. EBITDA margin has never been above 9% in twelve years: it was 9.0% in FY21, fell to 5.6% in FY23 when maize and soymeal spiked and Astec turned down, and recovered to 8.4% in FY26 on oil palm. Profit attributable to shareholders was ₹314 cr in FY21, ₹302 cr in FY23 and ₹473 cr in FY26 (EPS ₹16.3 → ₹15.7 → ₹24.6). Q1FY27 broke the run: revenue +9%, EBITDA ₹240 cr vs ₹270 cr, attributable profit ₹134 cr vs ₹161 cr, as crop care fell after a dry June.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a collection of low-margin, commodity-linked businesses (feed, dairy, poultry) attached to two high-margin ones (oil palm and crop care) whose profits swing with palm-oil prices and the monsoon. Over FY21-26 the group grew profit ~8.5% a year; the FY26 record owed much to war-inflated palm-oil prices. The new management's job is to make the mix better, not just bigger.

sections.title: Cash went into minority buyouts as much as into plants; returns improved mostly through working capital

blocks.p: In FY19-22 Godrej Agrovet generated ₹566 cr of operating cash, less than the ₹1,066 cr it spent on capex plus ₹449 cr of dividends: borrowings rose from ₹398 cr to ₹1,599 cr. In FY23-26 operating cash jumped to ₹3,802 cr, but about ₹1,030 cr of it (FY25-26) came from a rise in trade payables, much of it supplier financing. Capex was ₹1,265 cr. The other big use was buying out partners: ₹323 cr for Tyson's 49% of Godrej Foods (Aug-2024) and ₹922 cr for 47.9% of Creamline Dairy (FY25-26), plus ₹199 cr into Astec's rights issue. ROCE (Screener) recovered from 10% (FY23) to 19% (FY26).

blocks.callout: **The test is FY27-29.** Management now promises discipline: capex of ~₹400 cr in FY27 and ₹300-350 cr a year after, half of it in oil palm, projects only above a 16-18% IRR, and no further big buyouts announced. The buyouts did not add revenue (the businesses were already consolidated); they moved minorities' share of profit to GAVL's shareholders. Creamline earned ₹3 cr of profit in FY26, so ₹718 cr bought very little profit today.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but working capital, buyouts and one-offs need adjusting

bullets: **Supplier financing flatters cash flow.** Operating cash flow was ₹1,281 cr in FY26 against ₹864 cr of EBITDA, because trade payables rose ₹766 cr as Animal Nutrition moved to vendor invoice discounting. The financing cost now sits in segment costs, not interest (Q1FY27: reported feed EBIT ₹84 cr vs ₹102 cr "underlying"). Treat part of the payables as debt: on our reading net debt plus supplier credit is well above the reported ₹1,157 cr (the split is not disclosed).

**Buyouts shrink equity and lift ROE.** ₹953 cr paid above book value for the Godrej Foods and Creamline minorities went straight to equity (AR FY26 note 55B). ROE rose to 21% in FY26 partly because the denominator fell. CRISIL notes the hit to net worth and the rise in adjusted gearing to 0.81x.

**One-offs both ways in FY26.** Land-sale gains of ~₹34 cr sat inside EBITDA (company EBITDA ₹969 cr reported, ₹936 cr underlying); a ₹30 cr labour-code charge was exceptional. FY25 had a ₹15 cr long-term-incentive reversal. Company "EBITDA" includes other income; Screener's (₹864 cr, our model basis) does not.

**Other income inside segments.** ~₹9.5 cr a quarter of pet-food manufacturing income for Godrej Pet Care (a group company) is booked in other income but included in the Animal Nutrition segment result. We neutralise it through central costs in the model.

**Minorities run the "wrong" way.** Astec's minorities absorb a third of its losses, so attributable profit exceeded total profit by ₹28 cr in FY26. Screener's headline "Net Profit" (₹445 cr) and EPS (₹24.58 on ₹473 cr) are on different bases; we use attributable throughout.

**Related parties are small but real.** Sales to Godrej Industries ₹66 cr and to Godrej Pet Care ₹19 cr; expenses charged by Godrej Industries ₹25 cr (₹17 cr in FY25); dividends of ₹137 cr paid to the parent and ₹70 cr received from the ACI JV (FY26).
**Audit.** BSR & Co. (KPMG network); no qualifications; contingent liabilities ₹165 cr, mostly old excise disputes. Brands and goodwill (~₹320 cr) are not amortised and were not impaired in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing suggests aggressive revenue recognition, and the auditor is clean. But three things make reported numbers look better than the underlying business: supplier financing in working capital, ROE inflated by buyouts charged to equity, and FY26 one-off land gains inside EBITDA. Our forecasts use Screener's EBITDA (no other income), attributable profit, and assume supplier credit stays at the Mar-26 level.

sections.title: Moderate debt, and a working-capital gain that suppliers' banks are funding

blocks.p: Net debt was ₹1,157 cr at Mar-2026 (borrowings ₹1,574 cr incl. ₹106 cr of leases, less cash ₹302 cr and investments ₹115 cr, which include the ACI JV at ₹91 cr), about 1.3x EBITDA. CRISIL rates the commercial paper A1+ and puts adjusted gearing at 0.81x (0.57x a year earlier) after the Creamline buyout. The company reports average net working capital down from 45 days (FY24) to 25 days (FY26) and 21 days in Q1FY27. Much of that is trade payables, which rose from ₹628 cr to ₹1,651 cr in two years: Animal Nutrition now uses vendor invoice discounting, i.e. its suppliers are paid early by banks and GAVL pays the banks later. That is cheap funding, but it is debt-like and can be withdrawn.

sections.title: Ownership: a Godrej Industries subsidiary with a thin institutional following

blocks.p: Godrej Industries Ltd owns 65.05% and members and trusts of the Nadir and Adi Godrej families another ~2.7%: promoters 67.75% in Jun-2026, with no pledge reported. The 6.5-point drop in Dec-2024 was not a sale: after the 2024 Godrej family realignment, the holdings of the Jamshyd and Smita Godrej branch (now the separate Godrej Enterprises Group) were reclassified from promoter to public. Institutions own little: FIIs 6.48% (Temasek's V-Sciences 2.43%, down from 4.49% in Sep-2024) and DIIs 5.28% (Nippon India 2.09%, LIC 1.21%).

sections.title: Our forecasts: ~17% EPS growth after a soft FY27, below the street

blocks.p: We forecast each segment's revenue and EBITDA margin (segment result plus its depreciation), remove inter-segment sales and deduct central costs of ₹300-320 cr (which also absorb the other income that sits inside segment results). sections.title: The street: all Buys, with targets cut by a third in a year

blocks.p: Latest call per broker standing on 30-Sep-2026: three Buys (Motilal Oswal ₹675 after Q1FY27; ICICI Securities ₹900 and FundsIndia ₹683 from May-2026, before Q1). Targets have fallen from ₹940-980 a year earlier. No Sell or Hold found. BP Equities published a Q1FY27 result update on 7-Aug-2026 (Trendlyne); its rating and target were not visible without a login. The bull case is a turnaround story: a new CEO simplifying a sprawling portfolio, oil palm's maturing plantations and downstream push, crop care diversification, Astec's CDMO recovery and branded foods. We agree with the direction. Our disagreement is about how much of it is already in FY26 profit (war-time palm-oil prices) and how fast the weak businesses (dairy, foods, Astec) earn their cost of capital.

blocks.p: House rule: start from the stock's own one-year-forward multiple since Apr-2021, leaving out trough years (forward earnings a loss or below half the best of the previous three years). There are none for GAVL: the worst year, FY23, still earned 75% of FY22. The forward P/E median is 26.5x and the forward EV/EBITDA median 15.4x. Then we cut for how far comparable stocks have de-rated by 30-Sep-2026. EV/EBITDA is the street's yardstick and the one our SOTP uses; P/E is our relative cross-check.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better-run company than three years ago, fairly priced

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest cattle-feed maker and largest crude palm oil producer, a high-margin but narrow crop-care brand, a loss-making listed chemicals subsidiary, a sub-scale dairy and a young chicken brand, run by a new CEO who is pruning the portfolio. Two businesses earn ~70% of the profit, and both depend on prices the company does not set: maize and soymeal for feed, world palm-oil prices and Indian import duties for oil palm. The stock has returned nothing over five years (₹624 vs ~₹630-650 in late Sep-2021, plus dividends).

**What you are paying:** 19.6x our FY28E EPS (our SOTP applies 11.4x Sep-28E EBITDA to the businesses), against a forward P/E median of 26.5x and forward EV/EBITDA median of 15.4x since 2021. Our target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). The upside needs the weak businesses to recover and palm-oil margins to hold up better than we assume.

**Turn positive (BUY) below ~₹600**, or on evidence that crop care and Astec recover while oil-palm margins hold near 20% after the duty cut. **Turn negative above ~₹730** without an earnings upgrade.
**Biggest swing factor:** the CPO price. Our FY28-29E oil-palm margin of 19.5% is below FY26's 21.4% but above FY21's 15.4%; a return to FY21 margins would remove ~₹3.9 of FY28E EPS.
**Second swing factor:** the multiple. The street uses ~10-11x; the stock's own history says ~15x before the sector de-rating. At bull multiples (+2x) on base earnings the SOTP would be ~₹804.

sections.title: Glossary

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: Factory-made animal feed mixing grains (maize), oilmeals (soymeal), minerals and additives to a formula.
Fresh fruit bunches: the fruit of the oil palm, bought from farmers and crushed within a day.
Crude palm oil (from the fruit flesh) and palm kernel oil (from the seed).
Oil extraction ratio: tonnes of oil per tonne of FFB processed (18.8% in Q1FY27).
An area allotted by a state government to one processor, which must buy the FFB grown there at the state-set price.
National Mission on Edible Oils (Oil Palm): central scheme subsidising oil palm planting to cut imports.
Import tax on edible oils; with cesses, the effective rate on crude palm oil fell from 16.5% to 11% on 24-Sep-2026.
Crop protection products made from the company's own registrations vs products licensed from other companies (lower margins).
Contract development and manufacturing for other companies (Astec's growth focus).
Value-added dairy products (curd, paneer, flavoured milk), with higher margins than liquid milk.
Chickens sold live to traders vs branded packaged products sold to consumers.
Banks pay the company's suppliers early and the company pays the bank later; a form of short-term debt shown as payables.
The share of a subsidiary's profit or loss belonging to its other shareholders (32.97% of Astec).
Segment profit before interest and tax (result); EBITDA adds back the segment's depreciation.
Sum of the parts: valuing each business separately and adding them up, less net debt.
Enterprise value (market value + net debt) ÷ EBITDA; share price ÷ earnings per share.
A cut to the market value of a listed stake held through a parent (20% for Astec in our base case).
Discounted cash flow; WACC is the weighted average cost of debt and equity (~11.9% here).
A year whose forward earnings were a loss or below half the best of the previous three; left out of multiple medians.
